title: Phonograph records and Louis Armstrong as idol
summary: His father bought a phonograph; Cootie listened only to Louis Armstrong, learned the records by heart, and says Louis was his idol.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Oh, that was good. Well then I'm bringing it up to -- because I know that you went to the carnival. Your father took you and you heard Lester and Lee Young's father's band and everything. And I know you went there. But just before we talk about that, didn't you -- well, first of all, did you have a phonograph in the house?
Yeah. Uh-huh.
Your father had got a phonograph.
Yeah.
Well, did your brothers like to listen to Louis Armstrong? and so on? Did other people get those records?
Well, no. They wasn't particular about music. During that era. They had give it up.
Well, where did you get the records? Did you buy them?
Yeah, I would get them or my father would get them.
Oh. Well, did your father like that music?
Yeah.
Oh, he did.
Yeah, my father liked that music.
And then you'd get the records, too.
Yeah.
Who else did you listen to? You listened to Louis. Did you listen to Bessie?
No. I didn't listen to singers.
You didn't.
I was only interested in trumpets.
Is that right? Well, did you -- did you listen to King Oliver, then?
Yes. I listened to him, but not on records. I listened to King Oliver in later years on records, but during that period of time, I only listened to Louis.

Yeah.

I think his wife was playing the piano on them.
Oh, yeah. Yeah, I see. Lil.
Uh-huh.
Yeah. So that was when he was in Chicago, in those early days.
Yeah.
Yeah. Oh, so you knew those records backwards, don't you, Cootie?
Yeah.
Did you blow them? Did you get it down?
Yeah.
You blew it.
Uh-huh.

Yeah. Well, what did you -- did you feel a terrific excitement? I know you must have, because you've been absolutely wrapped up in music all your life. I want you to tell me how it felt when you first found you were -- well,
what was your -- what did you feel when you first heard those Louis records? You must have had a big feeling, didn't you?
Yes.
Did you run a temperature or something?
Yes. I thought he was the greatest thing I ever heard.
Yeah.
You know?
Yeah. You mean that beat.
Yeah. And that sound.
And that sound.
Yeah.
Yeah. Well, I guess that you knew right then that was going to be it for you always, huh?
Yeah.
Did you?
Yeah.
It didn't grow on you. You did know it for sure?
Yeah. Well, nearly everyone had an idol. And he was my idol.
